title: John Mack's abductee interviews at Harvard

tellings.quote: You have a predecessor at Harvard, a guy named John Mack, who was head of the the psychiatry department, who looked into kind of alien abduction stuff on a more of an anecdotal, kind of personal level.
He was actually a private clinician. He started to see people who would bring up these alien encounters.
tellings.difference: This telling calls Mack a private clinician whose patients brought up alien encounters on their own, rather than the head of psychiatry looking into abduction, and it also credits Thomas Kuhn.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings are about John Mack's own work at Harvard in the 1990s, hearing alien abduction and encounter accounts from people one on one, at an anecdotal and personal level. The Kuhn-encouraged 'Harvard study' story is about his whole late-career program, which is a broader grain.

plain: In the 1990s a Harvard psychiatrist named John Mack is said to have looked into people's stories of being abducted by aliens, working on a personal, case-by-case level rather than as a lab study. Michels tells this himself, first to the Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb, calling Mack his 'predecessor' and the head of the psychiatry department. In a later episode he tells it differently: Mack was a private clinician whose patients began bringing up alien encounters on their own, and Michels also links the story to the historian of science Thomas Kuhn.
